interventions.body:
Expert 1 here — the classifier that reads the structured panel and nothing else. My bid:

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.83
  uncertainty  +/- 0.09 epistemic (95% band 0.66-1.00); among patients I cannot tell apart the outcome was 0.66 of 1.00 mixed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 88% of the time over the 33 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most, across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, PI-RADS >= 4, no prior biopsy, pmhx_hypercholesterolaemia, suspicious DRE, number of comorbidities. I read 39 variables, all
from the panel — nothing from the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the previous notes or the
laboratory. Out-of-fold over 91 labelled cases: AUC 0.758, balanced
accuracy 0.625.

The final call is the chair's.

interventions.body:
This patient's situation: never biopsied. My criterion answers BIOPSY.

The criterion: sample when the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion; defer at PI-RADS 1-2. In the labelled series this criterion matched the reading urologist in 24 of 24 cases in exactly this situation.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines suggest that a PI-RADS score of 3 or higher is used to trigger a prostate biopsy. The guideline states, "a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger biopsy [135, 226, 264, 375], at the cost of missing a small number of mainly ISUP GG 2 cancers, especially in biopsy-naive patients or in highly selected populations with high prevalence of csPCa (in which the MRI NPV decreases) [372, 472]."

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED, your suggestion of biopsy is contradicted by the cohort criterion which states that the criterion matches the reading urologist in 24 of 24 cases in this exact situation. EXPERT-LIBRARY suggests a clear recommendation for biopsy based on similar PI-RADS 5 cases, which may differ from this patient's clinical context.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the prior biopsy status: None - the guideline suggests biopsy is triggered by PI-RADS $\ge 3$, and the patient is biopsy-naive, meaning the decision hinges on the PI-RADS score.
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: unchanged does not support re-sampling, new or larger does
psa_trend - the PSA trend: the guideline does not provide a specific threshold for PSA trend in this context, so the decision must rely on the PI-RADS score.
laboratory_results - the laboratory results: the guideline links PI-RADS scores to the decision, and the PI-RADS 5 score is the key factor here.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (clear). Last value 24.00 ng/mL over 3 points spanning 29 months; velocity +4.97 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 29 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 89.0 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 25.5-310.4.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.81
  uncertainty  +/- 0.07 epistemic (95% band 0.67-0.95), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

data.gist: Expert 3 suggests BIOPSY, p=0.81 +/- 0.07, HIGH reliability (firm, fusion_nolab)

interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents retrieved by the registrar appear to have answered the moderator's questions, as the `radiology_report`, `psa_trend`, and `previous_notes` were all retrieved.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence, specifically the PI-RADS 5 score from the report and the PSA trend showing a significant rise, aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's decision of BIOPSY, which was driven by the cohort criterion ($\text{PI-RADS} \ge 3$).

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What does the radiology_report state regarding whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study? The report states: "Study requested for anatomical localisation and staging."
Q2. What does the psa_trend indicate regarding the decision, given the guideline does not specify a PSA trend threshold? The PSA trend shows a rise from "11.8 (Sep 2022)" to "24.0 (Feb 2025)", indicating a significant upward trajectory.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 5 score is the most decisive variable as it directly triggers the EAU guideline threshold ($\ge 3$). The PSA trend is also highly relevant as it demonstrates disease progression, which supports the need for intervention.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a biopsy, as the retrieved evidence strongly supports the panel's conclusion based on the PI-RADS score and the rising PSA trajectory.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
